data.hypothesis: An eight-output chunk amortizes the nine initial row loads plus seven entering-row loads across eight outputs (about two samples per output rather than three for the four-output parent), while retaining a nine-value rolling register window and adjacent-X warp accesses. The longer per-thread work, unrolled loop, and reduced grid/thread count may instead hurt occupancy or scheduling, so the official oracle and timings must decide.

memory_lessons.applicability: The observed differences are modest and do not establish that chunk size caused the timing changes or generalizes beyond this workload.
memory_lessons.claim: The valid two-output experiment measured 3.4212 µs mean, the valid four-output parent measured 3.4491 µs, and the valid baseline measured 3.5815 µs; all three passed correctness in the supplied observations.
memory_lessons.next_experiment: Run the oracle and repeated official full-run timings for this eight-output candidate against the baseline and existing chunk-size candidates.

data.notes: The supplied catalog has two distinct valid programs: the two-output candidate is the measured best, narrowly ahead of four outputs; neither observation proves a cause. This eight-output candidate is an unmeasured reuse-versus-thread-work contrast. No correctness or speedup is claimed before controller evaluation.
transformations: Changed the per-thread Y chunk from four to eight while retaining 32 adjacent X lanes and the single-kernel launch.
Kept the nine-sample register window and shifted it by one row between outputs, loading one entering row per shift; bounded stores to valid Y outputs.
Retained the supplied period-63 index adjustment exactly, including leaving coordinate 63 unchanged.
